description:
Prerequisite discovered by the fz-go4.18.21 diagnosis (2026-07-02). The correct fix for the arrival-order devirtualization bug — call-target identity = callee + ACTIVATION at the two coalesce sites (semantic.rs:142 same_call_target, jobs/semantic.rs:1732 emission merge) — is proven to kill the non-determinism (repr_seam deterministic in all modes; JIT/AOT go from 'no settled callable boundary' compile-error to RUNNING) but regresses baseline-green opaque_fn_value_join::interp ('callable 163 ambiguous across entries [14,15]'): the joined add_a/add_b callable is LEGITIMATELY polymorphic, and once its two activations stay distinct, interp's runtime dispatch (src/ir_interp/backend.rs:2600-2740) cannot disambiguate them — it resolves by activation-input TYPE OVERLAP, which is BRAND-BLIND at runtime by design (fz-bsx: runtime equality/matching is brand-blind; typing is brand-aware). Brand-only-distinct activations are runtime-indistinguishable by type.

FIX DIRECTION: the boxed-callable boundary must dispatch by the VALUE'S IDENTITY (which concrete closure value flowed — its function id / capture identity), not by type overlap. This is the fz-hwn.22 boxed-callable / fz-hwn.27 addressed-arrow territory: the boundary already knows the concrete resolution per flowed value on the compile side; the runtime seam must carry/select by it. After this lands, the two-site callee+activation fix (diff preserved in the session scratchpad from the .18.21 diagnosis) is small and safe. SEQUENCING: this blocks fz-go4.18.21's fix. Note the payoff stack: .18.21 fix -> repr_seam deterministic + JIT/AOT compile -> residual deterministic-wrong routes to the f98.14 boundary bug with a clean signal.
title: Value-identity dispatch at the boxed-callable boundary (prerequisite for variant-distinct call-target identity)
